When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Crash Index 1/10: price action calm, no systemic signals in realized markets vs VIX Spike Tier 2/4: options market pricing meaningful vol expansion, skew and backwardation both active
These measure different things. The crash index reads realized price history; VIX backwardation reads where the options market is paying for protection today. Backwardation with active skew means hedgers are loading near-term puts. Trust the VIX structure: options hedgers tend to price fear before it shows up in realized markets.
Today's tension
Options market is pricing vol expansion that realized price hasn't confirmed.
Bull
Crash Index sits at **1/10**, the regime is STABLE at **14**, and contrarian score is neutral at **32**. Korea is up **+2.0%** and ETH is up **+23.7%** over five days, showing risk appetite is alive outside US large-cap.
Bear
VIX backwardation and skew are both active, **46.51%** of cross-asset pairs are diverging with **18** bearish vs only **2** bullish, and the SPY-TLT correlation has shifted from **-0.02** to **+0.57**, breaking the traditional stock-bond hedge.
The tell: Whether HYG credit stress or yen safe-haven flow joins VIX backwardation to fire a confluence signal: that is the reading that confirms vol expansion is real.
AI read · Citrini · today's macro tape

The surface reads calm. Crash Index is at 1/10, regime is STABLE at score 14, contrarian score sits at 32 (neutral), and all three monitored confluences are inactive. Nothing in realized price action is flashing red. Beneath that surface, 46.51% of the 43 cross-asset pairs tracked are drifting off their historical correlations, the mother divergence score has hit 100 (the maximum), and the internal bias runs 18 bearish pairs vs 2 bullish. The options market has already moved: VIX backwardation is active, skew is active, giving you a Tier 2 out of 4 VIX spike probability at 60%. That gap between calm price and stressed internals is the position.

You carry hedges without abandoning exposure. The macro regime reads INFLATIONARY at only 45% confidence, barely above a coin flip. You can tilt toward duration shorts and real assets, but the thin conviction margin demands small size. No regime sits at 45% for long: incoming data will push it decisively above or below 50%, and that move is where sizing gets aggressive.

The reading that flips everything is a confluence activation. VIX backwardation is live, but none of its three amplifiers have joined: HYG credit stress, small-cap drawdown, and yen safe-haven flow are all quiet. When the first one fires, you get confirmation. Until then, hold the hedge, respect the calm price, and watch credit.

Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence means two assets that used to move together (or in a predictable inverse relationship) have stopped following that pattern. Correlation drift is the measure of how far that relationship has shifted from its historical norm.

Right now 46.51% of the 43 cross-asset pairs tracked are in that drifting state, the net bias is 18 bearish vs 2 bullish, and the mother jaws composite score is at 100, the maximum. The most consequential dislocation: the SPY-TLT 60-day correlation has shifted from -0.02 to +0.57, meaning stocks and long bonds are now falling together and the traditional portfolio hedge has broken down.

The yield curve pair (t10y2y) flipped from +0.66 to -0.24, bond vol (MOVE) reversed from +0.87 to -0.20, and consumer discretionary vs staples (XLY vs XLP) shifted from +0.38 to -0.20. When this many relationships break across rates, vol, and sector rotation simultaneously, it signals a macro regime restructuring that hasn't yet confirmed in prices.

Asia · Europe · US · Crypto 24/7 — lead-lag detection
Cross-Region Surveillance
Major indices from the 4 regions/asset classes. Asia trades ahead time-wise vs US — a Tokyo overnight crash often leaks into the SPX open. Crypto = 24h leading indicator of global risk appetite.
AI read · the cross-region tape

The five-day cross-region equity picture is almost uniformly negative. In Asia, Korea's KOSPI leads at +2.0% while the Nikkei has shed -3.3%, a wide spread inside a single region that signals idiosyncratic stress in Japan rather than a broad Asian move.

Europe offers no relief: Switzerland's SMI is the region's best performer at -0.4%, France's CAC has dropped -2.0%. In the US, the NDX is off -2.9% over five days, lagging even the small-cap RUT at -2.0%.

Growth underperforming small caps in a risk-off period typically signals rate expectations are repricing higher rather than a broad flight from risk. Against all that, ETH's +23.7% and BTC's +15.9% five-day surge stand apart entirely: crypto is trading independently of equities, and ETH's outperformance over BTC points to elevated speculative appetite inside digital assets specifically.

Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 1/10 · WATCH — 1-2 signals, monitoring
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

Crash Index at 1/10 and VIX Spike Tier 2 out of 4 read different things entirely. The crash index measures realized price signals, what has already happened in markets.

The VIX structure measures what the options market is paying for right now. Active backwardation means near-term implied vol is priced above longer-dated vol, the structure you see when hedgers are loading front-end protection ahead of an expected move.

Active skew means puts are bid relative to calls on the same tenor. Together they say the options market smells a move that hasn't appeared in realized prices yet.

Given that the correlation architecture underneath is deeply dislocated (mother jaws at 100, 46.51% of pairs drifting with 18 bearish vs 2 bullish), the options market has the better read.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 1/10, so the tape is calm and there is no crash setup.

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
